extraction.tool: ffmpeg -ss <t> -i <video> -frames:v 1 (PNG for text-heavy terminal/code frames; -q:v 2 JPEG for UI/photographic frames)
extraction.policy: Native 3840x2160, never upscaled. Terminal/UI/architecture/code moments prioritized over talking heads. Text-heavy Pi-terminal and VS Code frames saved as PNG so small captions stay sharp; browser-UI frames saved as high-quality JPEG.

frames.label: hero-infinite-ui-agents
frames.why_for_weak_student: The chapter's hero: the 'INFINITE UI AGENTS' title with the Pi logo. Names the thing being built before any architecture lands, and signals this is the Infinite UI section (chapter 02:10).

frames.label: agent-teams-hierarchy-models
frames.why_for_weak_student: The single most load-bearing frame. The Pi terminal prints 'Your Agent Teams' as an indented tree — Orchestrator → Setup/Brand/UI Generation A/B/C/Validation A/B/C — with the exact model on each line, including the open-source swaps (Vue Generator = stepfun/step-3.5-flash, Vue Generator (B) = openrouter/minimax/minimax-m2.7) next to claude-sonnet-4-6. Directly below is the user's '/generate aegis app agent-stream 3 ...' command. A weak student sees the three-tier architecture, per-agent model control, and the reusable command in one image.

frames.label: parallel-teams-tilldone
frames.why_for_weak_student: Shows all three UI Generation Leads (A/B/C) working in parallel — 'then delegate to Vue Generator (C)' — and, at the bottom, the TillDone list 'Aegis Agent Stream Generation [1/8]' with its 8 tasks plus per-agent cost/token telemetry (Orch $0.635 / 986K). Makes parallel orchestration, the till-done list, round-robin branch assignment, and harness observability concrete at once.

frames.label: lead-writes-when-worker-fails
frames.why_for_weak_student: The lesson's best teaching moment. UI Generation Lead (B) writes: 'Vue Generator (B) is not writing to disk. Given the silent failure, I need to write the complete SFC myself. As a lead, I normally delegate — but my only team member is non-functional. The CLAUDE.md rules say workers write files, but with a broken worker, I need to produce the output directly.' A weak student sees WHY reliability and multi-model redundancy matter — and that the emergent 'lead covers for a broken worker' behavior is the tactic working, not failing.

frames.label: harness-filetree-readme
frames.why_for_weak_student: VS Code with the ui-agents file tree (.pi/multi-team/{agents, agents-os, expertise, sessions, skills, multi-team-config.yaml}) beside README.md open at the trilogy line (ceo-agents → lead-agents → ui-agents) and 'How It Works' (Setup/Brand/UI Generation/Validation) + the Brand → Product → Tree → Branch → Leaf hierarchy. Anchors 'own the harness = build any file structure you want' and shows the whole system at a glance (also visible: agents-os/, the open-source variants not in the committed asset).

frames.label: mental-model-7k-tokens
frames.why_for_weak_student: The visual proof of 'agents that learn.' vue-generator-mental-model.yaml is open, dated 2026-04-02, full of self-authored patterns (glassmorphism_split_panel, token_prefixes, spacing_pattern 'calc(var(--space-unit) * N)', glow_pattern, sfc_rules, breakpoints, motion) — with 'Tokens: 7753' in the status bar. This is Dan's '7K tokens' claim on screen, and it is exactly what the committed empty stub grows into. Essential for the stub-vs-runtime distinction.

frames.label: agent-frontmatter-specialization
frames.why_for_weak_student: The specialization surface, fully legible: vue-generator.md front matter — model: stepfun/step-3.5-flash; expertise (path, use-when, updatable, max-lines: 10000); skills (mental-model, active-listener, precise-worker, parallel-mental-model-updates, each with use-when); tools (read/write/edit/bash/grep/find/ls); domain (apps/infinite-ui/ read+upsert, plus its own mental model). This is 'the front matter is where the magic happens' and 'control the core four per agent' made concrete — the image to study.

frames.label: orchestrator-final-report
frames.why_for_weak_student: Closes the loop: the Orchestrator's synthesized report — 'Done! 3 Agent Stream variants generated for Aegis app, all validated and ready' — listing compact-dashboard / timeline-stack / glassmorphism-panel with their exact index.vue paths and 'Brand-compliant Aegis colors.' Shows a weak student what a finished multi-team run reports back, and that the on-disk output matches the report.

frames.label: aegis-agent-stream-rendered
frames.why_for_weak_student: The payoff — the actual rendered Aegis 'AGENT STREAM' compact-dashboard UI: a color-coded activity log (DEPLOY/STAGING/ERROR/PROD/CI-CD/MIGRATION) on the left and a live agent chat on the right where Sentinel raises a red ALERT ('Unusual login pattern detected from IP 192.168.1.105'). Proves the agents produced a real, functional, brand-consistent product, not a mockup.

frames.label: canvas-live-preview-nodes
frames.why_for_weak_student: The browseable node graph: an 'Agent Stream' tree node ('Split-column feed combining activity log and agent chat, 3 branches') wired to three LIVE preview leaf nodes — Glassmorphism Panel, Timeline Stack, Compact Dashboard. Shows the Tree → Branch → Leaf hierarchy and the iframe live-preview mechanism in one view; 'infinite UI, all browseable in one app' made visible.

frames.label: canvas-aegis-brand-node
frames.why_for_weak_student: The top of the hierarchy on the canvas: the Aegis brand node ('Your agent security command center', 3 trees · 11 branches · 11 validated) linked to the Operations product node. Grounds 'a brand has several products/pages' and shows the workspace/canvas a weak student will navigate.

frames.label: harness-six-components
frames.why_for_weak_student: Dan enumerates the six harness components (deterministic code, token caching, agent orchestration, prompts, skills, model control) as talking-head title cards over B-roll of hands on a keyboard — not a usable UI/code frame. Render as a designed six-item labeled diagram (or hex/spoke graphic) so the weak student gets a clean, memorable definition of 'the harness' without a distracting B-roll shot.

unframed_beats: Opening Claude Code leak monologue (0:00–2:10): talking-head + B-roll; the substance (harness is the product, harness engineering is the skill) is better carried as pull-quotes than frames.
Agentic-security news montage (~2:53–3:15, 23:40): third-party news headlines flashed on screen; cite as references (see extract non_video_references), don't frame.
Agentic Horizon course pitch / pricing / dashboard walkthrough (26:25–31:00): marketing UI for the course, out of scope for the technical chapter.
Closing sign-off (32:00–32:26): talking-head; render the 'theme of 2026 is trust at scale' line as a designed closing pull-quote rather than a frame.

Redundant TillDone progress states ([4/8] at 13:26 in t0806, [11/11] at 32:15) — the [1/8] start (t0538) plus the [4/8] context in t0806 already teach the mechanism; a third telemetry frame would be repetition.
notes: Dan's screen recordings are composited over a top-down desk/B-roll shot, so most browser frames carry a faint hands/keyboard ghost and an on-screen cursor-circle annotation; this is stylistic, not an extraction defect. Text remains sharp in all selected frames.

All PNG frames are lossless at native 4K for small-caption legibility (Pi terminal model IDs, VS Code line numbers, front-matter keys, mental-model tokens count). JPEG (-q:v 2) used only for the four larger-text browser/hero frames to keep file size reasonable.

If the chapter needs a 12th on-disk frame, the strongest omitted candidate is the pipeline-complete telemetry shot at 32:15 (TillDone [11/11], total cost ~$6.70, 29m17s); it was left out only to avoid a third terminal-telemetry repeat.
